items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Willie engaged a Cuban bass player named Jose Riestra for the Knocke engagement... I forgot to mention that Bobby Martin had left when I joined Willie.

ctx.x: Johnny Mitchel, Burns, Joe Hayman, Ted Fields and myself were the most regular customer, of Berry's cafe and we must have drank at least a gallon and a half of Dortmund between us every night. I was actually getting a kick out of beer for the first time in my drinking life.

Louis Vola had played bass with Willie in "Chez Florence" but Willie engaged a Cuban bass player named Jose Riestra for the Knocke engagement and I forgot to mention that Bobby Martin had left when I joined Willie. I could understand a little French by now, but Riestra didn't speak English and his French had a Cuban accent which was very hard for me to dig. He was a fine solid bass player and a wonderful person.

The band had ordered a uniform of white suits before we left Paris which we received two weeks after we had started at the casino, and the first night we wore them, it seemed as though those uniforms lifted our spirits sky high because we played better than we had been it seems to me. Willie Lewis did most of the singing in the band, but I featured in a number called "The Music Goes Round and Round" because it was a number that tells about what happens on a trumpet when the valves are pushed down.
